summary: This is a development container configuration file that sets up a Docker-based development environment for a Docusaurus blog project. It specifies how the container should be built, what ports to expose, environment variables to set, and what VS Code extensions and settings to use for a consistent developer experience.

explanations.3: This tells the system that this project uses Docusaurus, which is a documentation site generator.
explanations.4: This points to a Docker Compose file that defines how the actual Docker containers should be built and run.
explanations.5: This sets the working directory inside the container to /opt/docusaurus, so commands run in that location by default.
explanations.6: The 'mounts' section defines what files and folders from your computer get connected to the container; think of these as bridges between your local machine and the container.
explanations.7: This line mounts your bash command history from your computer into the container so you keep the same history across sessions.
explanations.8: This gives the container access to Docker itself, allowing you to run Docker commands from inside the container.
explanations.9: This creates a named volume for node_modules so the dependencies are stored separately and persist between container restarts, speeding things up.
explanations.15: When port 3000 becomes available, automatically open it in your browser.
explanations.22: These are the port numbers that will be forwarded from the container to your computer so you can access the services.
explanations.27: Before the container is created, these commands set up directories and files needed by the development environment.
explanations.28: After the container is created, this fixes file permissions and runs a setup script to install dependencies.
explanations.30: This uses environment variables to set the container user based on your system's user and group IDs, maintaining proper file ownership.
explanations.34: These settings apply only when you're editing Markdown files, keeping your Markdown formatting consistent and readable.
explanations.38: This designates which tool VS Code should use to automatically format Markdown files when you save.
explanations.41: Markdown lines will be wrapped at 80 characters wide, which is a common readable line length for documentation.
explanations.44: The spell checker is configured to check English language spelling.
explanations.57: These vertical lines appear at column positions 120 and 70 as visual guides to help you keep lines a reasonable length.
explanations.70: This tells the grammar checker to connect to a LanguageTool service running on port 8010 inside the container.
explanations.75: This configures bash as the default shell in the VS Code terminal that runs inside the container.
